





















                                         The Call

                                        Written by

                                        A. Writer































               A. Writer
               writer@example.com                              October 2026






               INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

               A small kitchen, cleaner than it needs to be. The wall clock
               reads 11:40.

               MARGARET (60s), cardigan buttoned wrong, sits at the table
               in front of a plate she hasn't touched. She watches the
               phone on the wall.

               SILENCE.
               Just the clock.

                                     MARGARET
                               (quietly)
                         You said you'd call.

               She scrapes the plate into the trash and sets it in the sink
               harder than she needs to.

               A KNOCK at the back door.

                                     DANNY (O.S.)
                         Mom? It's me. I lost my phone.

               Margaret doesn't move.

                                     MARGARET
                         Of course you did.

               She opens the door. DANNY (30s), soaked through, holds out a
               bakery box gone soft in the rain.

                                     DANNY
                         I did call. From a pay phone. Do
                         you know how hard it is to find a
                         pay phone?

                                     MARGARET
                         Harder than finding your mother's
                         house, apparently.

               He sets the box on the table and lifts the lid. Something
               that used to be a cake.

                                     MARGARET (CONT'D)
                         Is that a cake?

                                     DANNY
                         It was a cake.

               They both start talking at once.



                                                                         2.


                       MARGARET                        DANNY
               You can't just turn up at       I know, I know. I'm sorry.
               midnight with--                 I--

               They both stop. Margaret hands him a dish towel and, after a
               long moment, a fork.

                                                                    CUT TO:


               EXT. BACK PORCH - LATER

               The rain has stopped. Margaret and Danny sit on the step,
               eating the ruined cake straight from the box.

                                     DANNY
                         Next year I'll call from the
                         bakery.

                                     MARGARET
                         Next year you'll come at seven.

                                      END OF SAMPLE
